title: Switzerland hosts the Global Peace Summit on Ukraine at Bürgenstock
body:
Switzerland hosted a global peace summit on Ukraine on 15 and 16 June 2024 at the Bürgenstock resort near Lucerne. About 100 countries and organisations attended. Russia was not invited, and China did not attend. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took part in the plenary session on 15 June.

On 16 June, 78 states and four organisations signed the final joint communique. Several participants did not sign, among them India, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia, Colombia, South Africa, Thailand, Mexico and the United Arab Emirates. Other reports noted that Brazil attended as an observer and also did not sign. Countries that signed after the summit included Tonga, Barbados and Guyana. On 18 July 2024, speaking at the European Political Community Summit, Swiss President Viola Amherd said the communique had 87 signatories so far, and noted that some of the latecomers had not been present at the summit.

Amherd called the summit "the only initiative" with broad support across all continents and said participants had reached "a common vision" despite differing views. She said Switzerland would focus on strengthening ties with the Global South and China. Kyiv said it aimed to invite a Russian representative to a second conference to present a peace plan based on Zelensky's peace formula.
